reviews:
It's hard to ignore all the hype surrounding Fahmee Bakery and the story of what got them to this point, so when I happened to be at Scarborough's Malvern Mall, I had to stop in to try them for myself.

First impressions: the store is bright, spacious, and clean, with well stocked displays, and a friendly young lady providing good service.

I tried the Curry Goat Patty and their Apple Fritter. Both looked good but how did they taste?

The patty had a good looking crust, with squared off corners, rather than the traditional half-moon shape. It had a decent amount of filling. Not bad for $3.25.

With so many competitors in the Jamaican food scene, it's an uphill battle to stand out nowadays - even if you have the rights to a name that is beloved by the local community AND a strong social media presence.

There is potential here, but to me, it's clear they are still working things out: a true "2" at the moment, but I'm rounding up to 4 to support local businesses.

Regular price for a dozen patties is $28 but they had a promo where it's $24. That is still a smidge more pricey than some others but worth a shot, so off we went to try it!

As it currently is, Fahmees is a tale of 5 items.

Everything was so good, the waitress was so kind to answer our questions, beautiful and comfy interior, we can't wait to come back!
Small place, big flavor. Great to have an authentic Thai food near my workplace. Definitely recommended and will go back again for sure!

Newest addition to the cafe scene in Scarborough, located in the Lawrence and Warden plaza.

The strawberry cups are also well done, with a generous pistachio crunch and fresh strawberries dipped in chocolate and marshmallow.

The pizza here definitely has an authentic desi style. It smelled wonderful and the taste was quite good, featuring more interesting toppings and base sauce options than generic chains. I gave it four stars because it's genuinely better than places like Pizza Pizza and Domino's.

The Issue of Price and Texture
My main hesitation comes down to value. The overall taste was just "okay," and it wasn't quite up to the standard I expect for what is a premium-category price compared to the generic chains.

The BEST but also the most expensive bubble tea drinks, with average prices ~$8-10 before tax. Pricey but you do get what you pay for. Good for occasions.

Also loved the octopus plush sitting in the display today :)

Recently, they've been doing different combinations of their signature "pink salt cheese crema" drinks and they're pretty comparable to the mulberry one (which continues to be my favourite). Just be mindful that the strawberry one picture for example, is noticeably sweeter even at 0% sugar.

As well, parking in this plaza can often be a nightmare during busy hours, so plan ahead accordingly!

Pricier than most other bubble tea shops. I guess you get what you pay for in terms of quality. The pink salt cheese concoction is unique. Bubbles are soft and good quality too. Not a lot of places to sit at this location in Midland and Finch so more a take out place than anything.

Very happy to see TP Tea open in the area and the quality is on par with the Commerce Gate location. It's quite busy here which is a given the nature of the plaza but the operation is quite organized. Staff are efficient and fast.

We got the mango sago drink with tea jelly and a TP milk tea. The mango sago drink has a minimum ice level which was still a bit more ice chunks than I prefer but taste is great. The tea is actually quite strong and the pearls were standard, maybe nearing the edge of being overcooked.

Delicious and flavourful baos with unique flavors. The best bao we had was universally agreed to be vina chicken which had this juicy fried chicken with the Thai basil mayo. The kimchi on the bulgogi fries was a bit cold and would definitely benefit from stir frying it up. Would definitely come back to try the other baos as they all sound delicious.

At Bank Bao, you don’t just order food — you make a flavour investment. With walls decked out in bao puns and bao-branded merch, this spot is as adorable as it is delicious and trust us: the returns are very high.

The 5 Spice was a reliable blue-chip option, braised pork belly that felt rich, balanced, and always a safe bet. The Richie Duck was pure luxury stock — BBQ duck with hoisin-garlic mayo that tasted as premium as it sounds. Meanwhile, the Vina Chicken was a high-yield pick, crispy fried chicken paired with Thai basil mayo for a flavour payout that kept us coming back.

Bank bao was very good. The fried chicken was very fresh and hot. The toppings were also delicious. The BAO bun itself was very spongy and fresh. The place looks brand new - bright and shiny.
